source: INCOSE Guide to Writing Requirements V4 — Summary Sheet (INCOSE-TP-2010-006-04, June 2023)
note: Each rule lists the characteristics it supports per the V4 'Rules to Characteristics Cross Reference Matrix' (page 4). Transcribed from the provided Summary Sheet; confirm assessment-critical X marks against the original PDF.

rules.name: Structured Statements
rules.statement: Need and requirement statements must conform to one of the agreed patterns, resulting in a well-structured, complete statement.

rules.name: Active Voice
rules.statement: Use the active voice with the responsible entity clearly identified as the subject of the sentence.

rules.name: Appropriate Subject-Verb
rules.statement: Ensure the subject and verb of the statement are appropriate to the entity to which the statement refers.

rules.name: Defined Terms
rules.statement: Define all terms used within the statement in an associated glossary and/or data dictionary.

rules.name: Definite Articles
rules.statement: Use the definite article 'the' rather than the indefinite article 'a'.

rules.name: Common Units of Measure
rules.statement: When stating quantities, all numbers should have appropriate and consistent units of measure explicitly stated using a common measurement system.

rules.name: Vague Terms
rules.statement: Avoid vague quantifiers (some, any, several, many, about, approximate) and vague adjectives (relevant, significant, flexible, sufficient, adequate, appropriate, reasonable).

rules.name: Escape Clauses
rules.statement: Avoid escape clauses stating vague conditions or possibilities (as far as possible, where possible, if necessary, as appropriate, as required, to the extent practical).

rules.name: Open-Ended Clauses
rules.statement: Avoid open-ended, non-specific clauses such as 'including but not limited to', 'etc.', and 'and so on'.

rules.name: Superfluous Infinitives
rules.statement: Avoid superfluous infinitives such as 'to be designed to', 'to be able to', 'to be capable of', 'to enable', 'to allow'.

rules.name: Separate Clauses
rules.statement: Use a separate clause for each condition or qualification.

rules.name: Correct Grammar
rules.statement: Use correct grammar.

rules.name: Correct Spelling
rules.statement: Use correct spelling.

rules.name: Correct Punctuation
rules.statement: Use correct punctuation.

rules.name: Logical Expressions
rules.statement: Use a defined convention to express logical expressions such as '[X AND Y]', '[X OR Y]', '[X XOR Y]', 'NOT [X OR Y]'.

rules.name: Use of "Not"
rules.statement: Avoid the use of 'not'.

rules.name: Use of Oblique Symbol
rules.statement: Avoid the oblique ('/') symbol except in units (e.g. km/hr) or fractions.

rules.name: Single Thought Sentence
rules.statement: Write a single sentence that contains a single thought conditioned and qualified by relevant sub-clauses.

rules.name: Combinators
rules.statement: Avoid words that join or combine clauses, such as 'and', 'or', 'then', 'unless', 'but', 'as well as', 'however', 'otherwise'.

rules.name: Purpose Phrases
rules.statement: Avoid phrases that indicate the 'purpose of', 'intent of', or 'reason for' the statement.

rules.name: Parentheses
rules.statement: Avoid parentheses and brackets containing subordinate text.

rules.name: Enumeration
rules.statement: Enumerate sets explicitly instead of using a group noun to name the set.

rules.name: Supporting Diagram, Model, or ICD
rules.statement: When a need or requirement is related to complex behavior, refer to a supporting diagram, model, or ICD.

rules.name: Pronouns
rules.statement: Avoid the use of personal and indefinite pronouns.

rules.name: Headings
rules.statement: Avoid relying on headings to support explanation or understanding of the need or requirement.

rules.name: Absolutes
rules.statement: Avoid using unachievable absolutes such as 100% reliability, 100% availability, all, every, always, never.

rules.name: Explicit Conditions
rules.statement: State conditions' applicability explicitly instead of leaving applicability to be inferred from the context.

rules.name: Multiple Conditions
rules.statement: Express the propositional nature of a condition explicitly for a single action instead of giving lists of actions for a specific condition.

rules.name: Classification
rules.statement: Classify needs and requirements according to the aspects of the problem or system they address.

rules.name: Unique Expression
rules.statement: Express each need and requirement once and only once.

rules.name: Solution Free
rules.statement: Avoid stating implementation in a statement unless there is rationale for constraining the design.

rules.name: Universal Qualification
rules.statement: Use 'each' instead of 'all', 'any', or 'both' when universal quantification is intended.

rules.name: Range of Values
rules.statement: Define each quantity with a range of values appropriate to the entity and against which the entity will be verified or validated.

rules.name: Measurable Performance
rules.statement: Provide specific measurable performance targets appropriate to the entity and against which the entity will be verified.

rules.name: Temporal Dependencies
rules.statement: Define temporal dependencies explicitly instead of using indefinite temporal keywords such as 'eventually', 'until', 'before', 'after', 'once', 'simultaneous'.

rules.name: Consistent Terms and Units
rules.statement: Ensure each term and unit of measure used across the lifecycle is consistent with the project's defined ontology.

rules.name: Acronyms
rules.statement: If acronyms are used, they must be consistent throughout need and requirement sets and other SE artefacts across the lifecycle.

rules.name: Abbreviations
rules.statement: Avoid the use of abbreviations in needs and requirement statements and other SE lifecycle artefacts.

rules.name: Style Guide
rules.statement: Use a project-wide style guide for individual need statements and requirement statements.

rules.name: Decimal Format
rules.statement: Use a consistent format and number of significant digits for the specification of decimal numbers.

rules.name: Related Needs and Requirements
rules.statement: Group related needs and requirements together.

rules.name: Structured Sets
rules.statement: Conform to a defined structure or template for organizing sets of needs and requirements.
